title: Tensor products commute with colimits of modules
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ a small category (for instance a preordered set) and $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ a diagram of $R$-modules, with transition maps $M(a):M_i\to M_j$ for $a:i\to j$ (for a preordered set: $\mu_{ij}:M_i\to M_j$, $i\le j$), having a colimit $(M,(\mu_i:M_i\to M)_i)$ in the category of $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $N$ be an $R$-module. Then $M\otimes_RN$ with the $R$-linear maps $\mu_i\otimes1:M_i\otimes_RN\to M\otimes_RN$ is a colimit of the diagram $i\mapsto M_i\otimes_RN$ (transition maps $M(a)\otimes1$) in the category of $R$-modules; that is, the canonical map $\varinjlim_i(M_i\otimes_RN)\to(\varinjlim_iM_i)\otimes_RN$ induced by the $\mu_i\otimes1$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00DD (lemma-tensor-products-commute-with-limits, line 1934; stated for a system over a preordered set; first proof: $-\otimes_RN$ is left adjoint to $\operatorname{Hom}_R(N,-)$, Lemma Tag 00CV lemma-hom-from-tensor-product, hence commutes with all colimits; second, direct proof via Lemma Tag 00DA lemma-homomorphism-limit)
